When you get in sight of your destination you will see it surrounded by glowing energy rings.
Some missions will not require combat to complete them. But sometimes you just have to get that Fusion Spawn out of your way and reduce it to goo!

To engage in combat with a monster you must first target it by lining it up in your sights. Once you are aligned and within range, the monster's info window will appear at the top of your screen and battle brackets appear around the monster.
Click the Left Mouse button or press the "Z" key to fire (or swing) your weapon.
The first step is to choose a name  for your avatar. You can either use the name creation tool, or request a name you make up on your own.

As you inflict damage, the health of the monster will decrease. The monster's health is represented by the multicolor bar in the window in the top middle of the screen.  If the monster?s health drops to zero, the Fusion Matter that is animating the monster will break up, and the monster will disintegrate. You will automatically get any loot and items dropped by defeated enemies. To see the items you have collected (if any) open your inventory by pressing "I" on your keyboard. (See the section "Collecting Loot" in this document for more information.)
Monsters will make various types of attacks against you as well. If the monster has a special power an icon for that power will be displayed in the monster information screen.
If your health drops to zero, your character will be knocked out.
Some weapons (melee, shatterguns, etc.) can attack multiple targets at once. If your weapon is going to hit two or more targets, then each target that is in range will display a combat icon.

As mentioned before if you take damage you will lose health points. However you can get health points back by simply staying out of combat. After a bit of time your health bar will be fully restored and you will be ready to tackle Fuse's minions again.
Some Nanos have healing powers that can restore health to you (and sometimes your buddies), even when you are fighting.
The "Create Your Own" function allows  users to submit a name of their choice, subject to a screening process. You will be assigned a temporary name to use until your submitted name is approved.

If you get knocked out, your character will reappear at the closest Resurrect 'Em (graciously provided by Grim). However, your character may recover on the spot if you (or someone in your group) has a Revive power.
When you click the "Resurrect 'Em" button after being knocked out, you'll automatically reappear at the closest Resurrect ?Em.
Grim has opened Resurrect 'Em franchises all over the place. It shouldn't take long to get back to where you were fighting if this happens. Note that you will not return with full health.

Some Nanos have a Revive power. This power comes in two versions, one that works only on you and one that works for group members. If you have a "self-only" version of the power, you need to have the Nano up when you are defeated. When this happens, you are given the option to recover (at reduced health) at your current location.
If your Nano has the "group" version of the power and is active, any defeated players in your buddy group will be given the option to revive at their current location.
You can have two weapons equipped, but you can only use one at a time. Switch between weapons by pressing the "TAB" key.
There are six different types of weapons that you can collect.

* Rifle - ranged weapons that attack single targets.
* Pistol - ranged weapons that attack single targets.
* Shattergun - ranged weapon that attacks multiple targets.
* Rocket - ranged weapon that damages any monsters in the area where the missile lands.
* Melee - attacks any target right in front of the character.
* Thrown - weapon that damages any monsters in the area where it lands.

Each weapon is best suited for a different situation. Rifles and pistols are best against single opponents. If you are attacked by multiple monsters, Rockets or Melee weapons are best. If you don't know what enemy you'll be battling, Shatterguns and Thrown weapons are best.

Most weapons require you to have a target before they hit anything, but thrown and rocket weapons can be pointed anywhere and fired.  They explode when they hit something and any nearby targets are damaged. But, unlike other weapons, you will not see a targeting bracket.
Some monsters use a special attack called an Eruption attack. This will cause an explosion at your feet. These attacks are avoidable, but you have to be quick on your toes.
You can tell when an Eruption attack is coming -- the area under your feet will fill with green goo. If you react quickly, you can run away from the attack before the explosion occurs.

You can increase the damage that your weapon does by purchasing Weapon Boosts from a Shopkeeper. Each attack you make has increased power, but uses a number of Boosts based on the level of the weapon.
If you run low on boosts, a warning light will appear on your screen. Don't worry if you run out of Boosts -- you can still fight, you just do less damage.
Be careful with your weapon boosts. Some spawns have the power to drain the boosts you carry. You can counter this by having a Guard Nano active.

Nanos are small, collectible stylized versions of cartoon characters. Your Nanos assist you by boosting your stats and by providing special powers and abilities for combat and defense. (See the "Powers" section of this document for more information about Nano powers.) Nanos also provide specialized benefit in combat if you are fighting the right type of monster.
You can equip three Nanos in your NanoCom at a time, but you start the game with just one. Check out "Care and Feeding of Nanos" to learn how to make and equip a Nano to get your collection started.
The name creation tool lets you scroll through name combinations. To do this click and hold on the arrows. You can also randomly generate a name by clicking on the "Random" button.
A Nano's combat effects and powers only work when that Nano is summoned (active, or "up"). To summon a Nano, you simply hit its corresponding key -- 1, 2 or 3 -- as designated in the NanoCom.

The NanoCom shows three different attributes for each Nano:

* A/B/C type:  Whether the Nano is an Adaptium (A), Blastons (B), or Cosmix (C)
* Power: An icon showing which power it has and if it is ready to use.
* Stamina level: Displays how much stamina the Nano has regained while resting. A Nano cannot be summoned if it has no stamina.

Nanos cannot be active forever. Eventually, they get tired. They lose stamina while they are summoned, and lose additional stamina when using their powers. You have to give them a Nano Potion (see "Care and Feeding of Nanos") to restore their stamina or they will go away and rest for a while. The Nano stamina bar shows how soon your active Nano will need to rest.

Monsters and Nanos are divided into three types, each made out of a slightly different type of Fusion Matter - Adaptium (A), Blastons (B) or Cosmix (C). These different types trump one another very much like a game of rock/paper/scissors. So when you are fighting a monster, you should pay attention to what type of monster it is. The Nano you have active during combat can either help you or hurt you.
One you are happy with your name, click on "Continue". If the name is not already taken, you will proceed to the Character Creation screen.

You should always try to use a Nano that beats the monster type you are fighting. The monster's type is shown on the monster indicator on the top of your screen. The Nano's type is shown on the NanoCom in the lower-right of your screen.
Every once in a while, monsters will take a swipe at your Nano. This is called a Corruption attack.
Monster Ready to Make a Corruption Attack

When a monster does attack your Nano, they will wind up first, and then throw an attack that will trump your Nano. If you are fast you can drop your current Nano and bring out one that defeats the attack.  If your active Nano type beats the attack, the Nano will get a boost in stamina, protect your character from damage and send back a small damage attack to the monster. If the Nano loses, they will lose a lot of stamina. If you haven't summoned a Nano, you take the damage directly.

When a Nano is summoned, you can use its powers. Some powers automatically work as long as the Nano is active (auto powers). These include powers like Run and Jump boosts. Other powers require you to activate them (active powers). Stun, Heal, and Recover are examples. To use active powers, click the right button on your mouse or press the "X" key.
There are 108 different powers, but they are organized into 20 different types. You can tell what type of power your Nano has by looking at the icon associated with the power.

* Point -  affects a single target.
* Cone - affects multiple targets in an area in front of the user.
* Area - affects multiple targets in a circle around the user.
* Self - only affects the user.
* Group - affects all of the members in a group if nearby.

When you use a power you have to wait a brief period of time before it can be used again. When you use a power on a Nano, the power icon next to it on the Nano wheel will turn dark. It will turn bright again, once the power is ready to use.
While summoned Nanos will leave to rest when their stamina drops to zero, you can keep them active by using a Nano Potion. To use a Nano Potion, press the "C" key.
You can only carry a limited number of potions. Potions can be purchased from a Shopkeeper in the Cul-de-Sac and from other Shopkeepers around the world.
Be careful with your Nano potions. Some spawns have the power to drain the potions you carry. You can counter this by having a Guard Nano active.

After you have named your character, you will get to select your character's skin color, eyes, hair style, and clothing. Once you are happy with the way your avatar looks, click the "Continue" button. You will be asked to confirm your decision. Clicking "Yes" will launch the game.

Please note that while you currently are not able to edit your avatar past initial character creation, the ability to adjust your character’s features is something we intend to add in the future.

When you defeat monsters, you might get cash (Taros), Fusion Matter or a C.R.A.T.E.(Contains Really Awesome Things for Everyone) with an item in it. The loot and cash automatically goes to your character when you defeat a monster (see "C.R.A.T.E.S." below). Fusion Matter is used to create Nanos.
Coco is helping the war effort by laying eggs all over the world. These eggs are very valuable, containing power-ups that will boost your character for a short period.
Power-ups can make you run faster, show you nearby enemies, or enable you to jump higher.
If you see an egg, simply run over it. You will automatically pick it up and the power-up is immediately granted.
Some of Coco's eggs contain items. These eggs will be placed directly into your pack when you get them.

C.R.A.T.E.s contain supplies from the KND. In most cases, monsters have looted them from somewhere and will drop them when defeated in battle. You can also find them scattered around the world like Coco's Eggs.  You can't see what they hold when you find them, but you can tell the quality of item they will drop based on their type.
There are FOUR types of C.R.A.T.E.s -Standard, Special, Sooper and Sooper Duper. Standard C.R.A.T.E.s contain the most common items, but the best stuff can be found in the Sooper Duper ones.
C.R.A.T.E.s are also awarded for helping to clean up Infected Zones and completing missions.
You open a C.R.A.T.E. by first opening your pack (press the I key) and then clicking on the C.R.A.T.E. You can also trade unopened crates with other players.
Taros are the currency of the world. You collect them by defeating monsters, completing missions, and by helping clean up the infected areas of the world.
You can spend Taros at shopkeepers to buy items, potions and boosts. You can also use them to pay for Warps and flights

While Fuse's minions are found all over the world, there are some places where they have really made an impact. These areas have been isolated by force fields to try to stop the spread of the Fusion Matter infection. Many missions will take you into these Infected Zones. You may also want to go in to help gather up raw Fusion Matter before the infection spreads further.
Greetings, I am Dexter’s robot assistant, Computress. I have taken the liberty of writing this field guide to help you better prepare for your fight against Fuse. I hope you find it useful.
Outside the Sweet Revenge Infected Zone
GETTING IN AND OUT OF INFECTED ZONES

Infected Zones have been isolated by SACT (the Special Alien Capture Team) using force field technology from Dexter.  You have to enter and exit them via a special warp gate. Warp gates are portals that transport players into and out of Infected Zones. To enter an Infected Zone, click on the Dexbot attendant at the gate and select the warp icon.  You exit the same way. Normally there are at least two ways out of any infected zone.

The Infected Zones are full of raw Fusion Matter that can hurt you. Stay out of the green pools of Fusion Matter if at all possible, or you will be poisoned and start taking damage. Even after you are no longer touching the raw Fusion Matter, your character will continue to take damage for a period of time.
These zones are also full of various devices, platforms and objects placed by SACT agents to help you navigate the area safely.
Jump Pads - Jumping on a jump pad will allow you to jump higher in the air than normal.
Zip Line - If you click on the end of a zip line you slide down to the end. You can let go of the zip line at any time by pressing the Space Bar. Some zip lines allow you to travel upwards as well.
Slide - Jumping on a slide allows you to move down a twisting slide to the bottom.  You can steer while sliding using normal commands.
Moving Platforms - You can ride a moving platform to traverse dangerous areas.
Launcher - Launchers are cannons that can shoot you out and over danger. Check out the table in the "Controls" section of this document to learn how to use the launcher.

After you complete character creation, you are sent back to Dexter and his time travel experiment. Unfortunately, Dee Dee sneaks into the lab and pushes the wrong button, sending you about six months into the future by mistake, and the time machine is destroyed. While in the Future, you discover that Fuse has invaded and has taken over most of the world. But all is not lost. If you can rebuild the time machine, you can go back to the past, bringing back the only things that will let our heroes win their war against Fuse; Nanos!
Some Nanos have an ability called Recall. Using this ability warps the player back to a special device called a Recall Portal.
To use a Recall Portal you first have to click on it to register it on your NanoCom. Then whenever you want to go back to that point, summon the appropriate Nano and use its recall power
You have to be inside an Infected Zone to use the Recall power. If you leave the Infected Zone the power will not work.
Note that you can use the recall power when you are cleaning up the infected zone (see "Cleaning Up Infected Zones" below).

The KND and SACT (Special Alien Capture Team) have set up stations in the Infected Zones to let you collect and dispose of newly created Pods. If the Pods aren't collected and disposed of, they will grow into Terrafusers and the Infected Zone will expand further. The collected Pods need to be disposed of quickly, so you'll need to run through the area scooping up as many as you can in as short a time as possible. When you reach the end, deposit the Pods in the drum provided by SACT.
As a reward for your Pod collection effort you'll receive refined Fusion Matter. Remember, you need that Fusion Matter to create more Nanos!
The basic commands to control your character are explained below. A full list of commands can be found at the end of this document for quick reference.

To begin collecting Pods, go to a starting station and check in. Once there, click on the attendant (usually a SACT agent) and you will be given the option of running the race or viewing the scores for this Infected Zone.

To finish the race, click on a finishing station (again, look for the SACT agent). You will be given your score and your reward of refined Fusion Matter, based on your time and the number of Pods collected.
There is a special class of monsters called Fusions. These are Fuse's top henchmen. They resemble the world's heroes and villains, but they have a definite evil streak.
Fusions hide out in the Infected Zones in treacherous lairs. These lairs are almost always located in Infected Zones, and sometimes are very difficult to reach.

To enter a Fusion Lair, find the lair and click on it just as if you were using a warp gate to get into an Infected Zone. If you have the right pass code or key you will be able to enter the lair and confront the Fusion.
Nano Missions are very special missions, and completing them is a good way to power up your character. Completing a Nano mission will reward your character with a new Nano and level you up.
You will be automatically assigned a Nano mission when you fill up your Fusion Mater meter, which can be done by defeating monsters, running races, and completing missions.

You can check on the Nanos you’ve collected by opening your Nano book. This can be accessed from your inventory, or by pressing the “N” key. Here, you’ll find a list of every Nano in the game, as well as information on what level you will become once you create them by completing their assigned Nano mission.

The first thing you need to learn is how to move around the world. You can either use the arrow keys, or use the mouse in conjunction with the WASD keys on the keyboard. The game also supports using a USB Controller, however you must still use a mouse to interact with menus.

Certain optional Nano missions will reward you with a Nano without leveling you up. These are known as World Nano missions, and are not automatically assigned when you collect enough Fusion Matter. These are instead given out by characters after certain criteria have been met. Generally, this will involve reaching a certain level and completing a specific set of missions.

Since you can only take on one Nano Mission in your journal at a time, accepting a World Nano mission will temporarily prevent you from being assigned the next Nano mission needed to level you up if you fill your Fusion Matter meter.

If you would like to cancel your World Nano mission and take on the required Nano mission instead, simply delete the World Nano mission from your journal and you will be assigned the required Nano mission shortly thereafter.

Nanos are collectible stylized versions of cartoon characters that assist players by giving them special abilities or boosts. Players can collect over 36 Nanos, but can only have three equipped at any given time.
Details on using Nanos in combat can be found in the "Nanos in Combat" section of this guide.

Directional movement is controlled with the W (forward), A (left), S (back), and D (right) keys, and the mouse will control both the camera. In this scheme, the left/right movement of the mouse "steers" the character to the left or right, as the camera moves. Moving the mouse forward and back allows you to look up and down.

To create a Nano, you must complete a Nano mission. You will automatically be given a Nano mission when your Fusion Matter meter is full, but certain characters may also give you Nano missions after special conditions are met.

As your new Nano is created, you must choose one of three possible powers for it. The power you select will affect the battles you enter with this Nano, so choose carefully! (Don't worry too much. If you don't like the power you chose, just use a Nano Station and some power items to change it -- see "Changing Powers.")
Your newly created Nano will be added to your Nano Book, which can be accessed from your inventory screen. You may also press the “N” key to open the Nano Book at any time.
The amount of Fusion Matter required to be assigned your next Nano mission increases each time you level up.

You can collect over 36 Nanos in FusionFall Retro. However, you can only equip three Nanos in your NanoCom at a time. You can only equip Nanos at a Nano Station. These can be found across the world, including locations like the Cul-De-Sac and the KND Treehouse.
To change out Nanos, click on the Nano Station.  Then select the Nano you want to equip from your Nano Book. You can equip it in the #1, #2, or #3 position of your NanoCom.

When you create your Nano you choose its power from a list of three possibilities. However, if you change your mind later, you can swap out that power for one of two other options. To do this, go to the Cul-de-Sac or another location with a Nano Station and click on the Nano you want to modify.

If you want to change the power of your Nano, you'll need to buy power items based on the type of power you want to activate (consult the Nano's power chart to see what power items you need to purchase). There are vendors near the Nano Stations that sell power items. You also will need to use some of the Fusion Matter you've collected.
Next go to a Nano Station, click on it and select the Nano you wish to modify from the pop-up interface. If you have enough power items and Fusion Matter, you can change the power of your Nano.

Gumballs give your Nanos short-term bursts of power. You will occasionally pick them up when defeating monsters. Gumballs are simple to use. Open up your inventory pack by pressing the I key, then click on the Gumball that you want to use. Next, select the Nano you wish to feed it to.
The Gumball will increase the effectiveness of the Nano for a short time (until the gum loses its flavor).

You can talk with other players using two methods, Menu Chat or Open Chat. You can use Menu Chat to say things "out loud" to players around you. Open Chat allows you to type whatever you wish as you chat with other players.
Unlike Menu Chat, Open Chat lets you type whatever message you like. This chat is monitored and filtered to ensure everyone has a good time.
To use Open Chat hit the "ENTER" key and select the Chat line under the communications log. Then just type whatever you want into the space and hit "ENTER" again to say it.
There are three communications channels in the game

* All - Heard by everyone nearby
* Group - Heard only by your group members
* Buddy - Heard only by your buddy
To select each channel just click on the tab above the communications log.

Menu Chat can be used by all players. It provides a set of pre-selected phrases that can be chosen from a drop-down menu. To use Menu Chat, simply hit the "ENTER" key and choose a phrase from the menu by clicking on it. To close the chat menu, press the "ENTER" key again.

This sounds more complex than it really is. If you want to go forward, just hold down the W key. Then, use the mouse to steer left and right as you run along. When you want to stop, just release the W key. It's just that simple.
Both Menu Chat and Open Chat can be used for chatting one-on-one, with a group, or with any players nearby.
To speak "out loud" to nearby players, simply use the chat functions as described in the "Menu Chat" and "Open Chat" sections above.
To send a buddy chat message to another player, you first have make that player your buddy. To do this, target the character and click on the buddy icon. This will add the player to your buddy list.

To send your new buddy a message, hit the "ENTER" key and select the Buddy tab by the Communications log. Select your buddy from your buddy list and select Send Message to send IMs back and forth, using either the Menu or Open Chat methods. You'll also be able to email your buddies in the game. (For more details on In-Game Email, please see the "Email" section of this document.)

To chat with a group, you must set up a group the same way you added another player to your buddy list. Instead of choosing the buddy icon when you click on other players, select the group icon. To send the group a message, hit the ENTER key and select the Group tab above the chat window. You can now send messages to everyone in your group at one time, using either the Menu or Open Chat methods.

To make your character jump hit the Spacebar. This is useful for climbing over obstacles and jumping across platforms. For more precision, you can also use the movement keys while in midair to adjust where you want to land.

Your character and Nano will perform emotes at your command. To use emotes, hit the ENTER key and select Emotes from the Menu Chat list. Then select the emote you want to your character and Nano to perform.
Players can form groups in FusionFall and use cooperative play to take on difficult enemies.
To form a group, target the player you want to group with and click on them. Then select the group icon.
To leave the group you have to hit the "ENTER" key and then select the "LEAVE GROUP" button above the communications log..
You can chat with just your group members by selecting the "Group" tab above the Communication log.
If you make another player your buddy, you can use the peer-to-peer chat system and Buddy Warping.

To make someone a buddy, click on the character and select the buddy invitation icon.  That will send an invitation to the other player. If he selects Yes from the invitation message, he becomes your buddy.

To send a buddy a message, hit the ENTER key and select the Buddy tab by the Communications Log. Select your buddy from your buddy list and select Send Message to send  IMs back and forth, using either the Menu or Open Chat methods.
You can also utilize your buddy list to move around the world. Once you've made another player your buddy, you'll be able to warp to him (with some restrictions) wherever he is in the game world.
To warp to a buddy, select the buddy from your buddy list and then select Warp. You will be immediately transferred to your buddy.
You will not be able to warp to your buddy if he is in an Infected Zone or Fusion Lair, or if you have recently used Buddy Warp.
FusionFall allows you to trade items with other players. To do this, click on the other player and select the trade icon.
If the other player agrees to trade with you, a trading window will appear.

The trade screen shows your offer and the other player's offer. To add an item to your offer, click on the item from your inventory and select "Add" from the item description window.  To remove an item, click on the item in the offer window and select the "Remove" option.
Taros (money) can also be traded by clicking on the Taros counter.
When you like the other player's offer, click the "Accept" button. If he also likes what you are offering, and has hit the "Accept" button, then the items and Taros are traded
Some items, such as guide rewards and mission items, cannot be traded.
You are also able to chat with the person you are trading with, just like normal, using either Open Chat or Menu Chat.
A word of warning: The world is full of Fuse’s infection! Avoid running through or swimming in these infected patches, since you will take damage from them.

You'll receive email from your guide periodically during the game. You can also receive email from buddies. When you get a new email message, a red envelope icon will light up on your Mini-Map. To open your email, hit "ENTER" and select Email from the menu, or just hit the "P" key.
The messages are on the left side of the screen and the text is displayed below them. To open an email and read the text, select the message by double clicking it.

To send an e-mail click the "Send Mail" button. From there select the buddy you want to send the e-mail to. Type in the subject and message you want, and then click the "Send" button. You can also send your buddy gifts, like items or taros.

You can group with up to 3 other players. To invite someone to group with you, you click on them, and then select the group icon. That player will get your invitation. If they accept you will see their HP bar appear on the left side of your screen. If they have a Nano active, then their Nano's name and stamina level are also shown.
Anyone in the group can invite someone else, but the maximum number of players allowed in a group is 4.
To chat in a group just hit "Enter" and select the "Group" tab, then chat as normal. Only the members of your group will see your chat.
To leave the group hit "Enter" and click on the red "Leave Group" button above the communications log.

Sometimes you want to just not listen to someone. You can ignore a player by clicking on the player and then clicking on the ignore icon. Once you do that, you are removed from their buddy list (if you were on it), and you can no longer hear their chat.
To remove someone from your ignore list, click on them and the click on the unignore icon.

There are many different ways of getting around the world. The simplest way is to just run to where you want to go. If you want to get to your destination more quickly, use the local transportation systems.

You character is equipped with a new invention from Dexlabs called the NanoCom. The NanoCom combines navigation, communications and Nano storage into one easy-to-use device. When using it, you'll see computer graphics superimposed over the world that will keep you informed as you battle the Planet Fusion invasion.

The S.C.A.M.P.E.R. and Monkey Skyway systems require that you register at both points in the network. For example, to use the S.C.A.M.P.E.R. between the Cul-de-Sac and City Station, you must register with both the S.C.A.M.P.E.R. attendant in the Cul-de-Sac and the attendant in City Station. It?s easy to find an attendant, because they have a transportation icon over their heads.
S.C.A.M.P.E.R.s transport you from one region to another. The long-range S.C.A.M.P.E.R system has four stations: Cul-de-Sac, City Station, Jungle Outpost and Forsaken Valley.
To use the S.C.A.M.P.E.R, click on the attendant and select your destination. There is a small fee for using a S.C.A.M.P.E.R.

The Monkey Skyway system was created by Mojo Jojo using his Monkey Minions. The Skyway is designed for shorter hops between neighborhoods in a region. Using the Skyway system, you are carried by your very own flying monkey to your destination. There are a number of Monkey Skyway stations in each region, but they don?t connect across region boundaries.
To use the Skyway, click on the attendant and select your destination. As is the case with S.C.A.M.P.E.R.s, there is a small fee for using the Skyway.

Vehicles are available for rent from shopkeepers throughout the world at Kevin's Hot Rod Rentals. Rental periods vary depending on the vehicle. Riding a vehicle allows you to travel around the world faster, and protects you from infected patches on the ground. You cannot fight Fuse's monsters while riding a vehicle. If you engage a monster in combat you will automatically dismount the vehicle you are riding. You will also automatically dismount if you attempt to interact with another player or NPC . Note that you cannot ride a vehicle inside an infected zone.
To equip a vehicle, simply open your inventory and equip the vehicle like you would equip any other piece of equipment. You can also mount/dismount your vehicle in the world by pressing the "V" key.
To learn more about vehicles, see the "Buying Stuff" section.

The Slider is a rail transportation system. It runs through the Suburbs and Downtown. Unlike the S.C.A.M.P.E.R. or Skyway, you don't need to register or pay to use the Slider. You also can get on or off at any point along the journey.
You have access to two different maps of the world to help you navigate: a world map that shows all of the regions, and a local map that displays the details of your current neighborhood
To call up the map, either hit "ENTER" and select "Map" from your menu, or hit "M" on your keyboard.

This map is an overhead view of your immediate area, fed directly through your NanoCom. It shows your position and any waypoints that you need to reach, as well as locations of other characters and devices that are helpful to you.
You can zoom in out or out of this map to see more or less detail. The satellite map does not work inside of Fusion Lairs

* Equipped Nano: Shows which Nanos you have equipped, what type they are, and if they have enough energy to be summoned. Next to them is a small icon showing their equipped power.

* Mini-Map: View of your immediate area from above.

* Fusion Matter Meter: Around the mini-map is a Fusion Matter meter that shows how much Fusion Matter you have stored up. Fill this meter all the way to automatically receive a Nano mission that will level you up when completed.

* Communication Log: A record of recent communications and events that have happened near you.

* Your Health:  Displays your health status.

* Active Nano: Shows the name, stamina and power of your active Nano.

* Effects:  Under your health bar, your temporary power-ups are displayed. These include pick up items like extra speed, jump boosts, or protection from certain types of attacks. See “Powers” for more details.
Once you have the character window open, you can equip items from your pack. Simply select the "Equipment" tab on the right side of the character window.

Click on the item you want to equip. A description window will pop up. Click on the "Equip" button and the item will appear on your character (assuming it is the right level and it is not a clothing item for the opposite gender). You can also click and drag items to equip them.
To unequip an item, click on the item in the center column to call up the item description window. Then just click the "Unequip" button.

Note that you can equip two weapons at a time. When you get the description window for a weapon, it will have two equip buttons - "Wpn 1" or "Wpn 2". Switch between the two weapons by using the "TAB" key on your keyboard.
The item description window shows five item attributes (seven for weapons):
Other informational graphics will pop up as the situation calls for it. Details on these are covered in the sections below.

* Stats - how much the item will boost your "vs. One", "vs. Many" and "Defense" ratings when equipped.
* Level (lvl) - the minimum level you need to be to equip the item.
* Description - the name of the item as well as a brief description about it.
* Type (weapons only) -  the type of weapon. Weapon types determine the range and the number of targets each weapon and hit.
* Range (weapons only) - The distance the weapon shoots.
* Cost - the resale value of the item to a Shopkeeper.
* Rarity - indicates if the item is Common, Uncommon, Rare or Ultra Rare. The greater an item's rarity, the better its stats.
Also note that some items are gender-specific. This restriction is normally part of the item name: "Techaneer Shirt (Girls)," "Gorey Boots (Boys)," etc.
There are 6 types of weapons available in the game. Each is best in a specific situation, so it is always good to equip two, based on what type of monsters you expect to fight.

* Rifles - long range. Best against single targets, poor against groups of spawns. Uses a target reticule.  
* Pistols - short range. Best against single targets, poor against groups of spawns. Uses a target reticule. 
* Shattergun - long range.  Good against single targets, good against groups of spawns. Uses a target reticule. 
* Melee - short range.  Good against single targets, good against groups of spawns. Uses a target reticule. 
* Rockets - long range. Poor against single targets, Best against groups of spawns. Does not use a target reticule. 
* Thrown - short range. Poor against single targets, Best against groups of spawns. Does not use a target reticule.
Some gear is worn just for fun.  Hats, backpacks and masks are all items that you put on just to show your personal style. As long as you are of the necessary level, you can wear an accessory.

Unlike armor (shoes, pants, shirts) you don't have to worry about wearing an accessory that is too low level. If you love that Chowder hat, you can wear it all the way to level 36 without having your combat effectiveness reduced.
You always have your My Stuff pack with you. You see what is in your pack by clicking the Equipment tab once you open your character window.  You can also hit the I key on your keyboard.

You can only carry a limited number of items in your pack. Since you get rewards automatically placed in your pack when you defeat monsters, you will want to make sure you have as many open spaces as possible before you go out adventuring. You can do this by selling unneeded items to a Shopkeeper, storing them in your bank vault or deleting them.
To delete an item from your pack, click and drag it to the trash can in the lower-right corner of the inventory screen. Note that once you do so, you will not be able to retrieve the item.
As mentioned above, if you have too much stuff in your pack, you can always store it in your bank vault. Everyone has one. It's one of the benefits of being a hero.
You have to go to a Banker to get to your vault.  There are Bankers in the Cul-de-Sac (Suburbs), Townsville Mall (Downtown) and the Jungle Outpost (Wilds).

Click on the Banker and select the bank icon. The bank window will pop up. Click on the items that you want to move between your bank vault and your pack. This will open an item screen that lets you switch to the bank or your pack.

The quickest way to find out about your character is to check out your character window. To open the character window (inventory), press the "I "button. Alternatively, you may hit ENTER and select "My Stuff" from the main menu.
You can also click and drag items between your vault and your pack.
You can see which Nanos you have and which ones you are developing (via a Nano mission) by clicking on the Nano tab once you are in the character screen.

Vehicles appear in your inventory along with all your other gear. You can equip a vehicle by selecting it from your inventory and clicking EQUIP. You can also review your vehicle's stats, including its speed rating and how much time remains in its rental period. When a vehicle's rental period expires, it will automatically be removed from your inventory.
To rent a vehicle, you need to talk to a shopkeeper at Kevin's Hot Rod Rentals. To learn more, see the "Buying Stuff" section.

Combining enables you to take the stats from one item and apply them to the look of another item, effectively changing the stats of your favorite items while preserving their looks. This process allows you to take items that you obtained earlier in the game and preserve/extend their usefulness for your character as you progress.
To combine items, you need to talk to a shopkeeper at the Croc Pot Catering Company. To learn more, see the "Buying Stuff" section.
Clicking on a Nano opens the description window for that Nano. The Nano window contains the following information:

* Type - lists the A/B/C type of the Nano.
* Current Power - displays the Nano's current active power.
*Other Powers - shows the other powers that the Nano could have, as well as the type of power items needed to change it. (See "Changing Powers" in the "Care and Feeding of Nanos" section of this guide.)
When you start the game, you will have two weapons as well as the basic clothing that you selected during Character Creation. You also will have a Buttercup Nano equipped in your NanoCom.
You can purchase other items at the KND Treehouse, and other locations throughout the world.

To buy something  go to a Shopkeeper and align your character to them. Most of the Shopkeepers have a holographic icon showing what type of items they sell. A shopping icon will appear when you are properly lined up.
Click on the Shopkeeper and an interaction menu will appear. Click on the top icon to open the sales window

Once the store interface is open, you can buy items from the Shopkeeper. Make sure you purchase Level 1 items at first since you will not be able to equip anything higher than that when you start in the game. As your character levels up, you'll be able to equip better and better gear.

Click on an item to bring up an information window about it. To purchase an item, click on the Buy button in the information window. If you don't have enough Taros, the game will not let you purchase the item.

You can sell an item from your pack (right side of the screen) to the Shopkeeper as well. Click on the item in your pack. The item description window will pop up and show you what the Shopkeeper will pay for it. If you like the price, click the "Sell" button, otherwise click the "Cancel" button.

If you sell something by mistake you can buy it back for exactly the same price that you got from the Shopkeeper by clicking on the Recent Sells tab and selecting the item you want back. The item is available for repurchase for a limited time, so make sure you buy it back quickly.
To leave this screen (or any screen like it) click the red button in the upper-right corner of the window.

This Egg Generating Gizmo Ejects Rewards! Fashioned to resemble the Imaginary Friend, Coco, this machine allows you to purchase an E.G.G. and the surprise accessory contained inside. When it comes to E.G.G.s, Everyone Gets Gear! You will find that E.G.G.s have different degrees of quality, and the most expensive E.G.G.s have the greatest likelihood of revealing a very special or ultra-rare accessory. Look for a Mystery E.G.G. to find the rarest of rewards.

E.G.G.E.R.s sell items across a number of level ranges, so check to make sure that you can use the item contained inside an E.G.G. before you purchase one. Once you have purchased an E.G.G., simply click on it in your inventory to open it and see what is inside. Different E.G.G.E.R.s sell different E.G.G.s (with different items inside), so be sure to visit them all.

Kevin's Hot Rod Rentals is the place to go to get  a vehicle. Vehicles allow you to get around faster, and come in a variety of speed classes and styles. You will also notice that you cannot add a vehicle to your inventory permanently; vehicles are only available for rent and for different rental periods. When a vehicle's rental period expires, it will automatically be removed from your inventory.
To equip a vehicle, select it from My Stuff and click on Equip. You can also hit the "V" key when in the world to mount/dismount your vehicles.

Some things to remember about vehicles:
- Vehicles protect you from toxic patches of Fusion Matter on the ground
- You cannot engage with monsters while riding a vehicle
- You cannot engage with other players or NPCs while riding a vehicle, but you can use chat
- Nanos and emotes cannot be used while riding a vehicle
- You cannot ride a vehicle inside an infected zone
- The Warp Away command is still available while riding a vehicle
To see how much time remains in a vehicle's rental period, simply select it in your inventory. The information appears in the detail pop-up about the item.
Your character will appear on the left, wearing and carrying all the items that you have equipped.

The shopkeepers at the Croc Pot Catering Company will help you combine two items into one by throwing them into their very special Croc Pot and mixing them together. Combining items allows you to take the look of one item and apply the stats from another item to create an entirely new item! (In other words, you preserve the original's look but change its stats.) This process allows you to take items that you obtained earlier in the game and preserve/extend their usefulness for your character as you progress.

It's simple: choose the item from your inventory with the STYLE you want and place it in the style slot. Then select the item with the STATS you want and place it in the stats slot. Note that you will also transfer the item's level.

Once you have placed both items, the shopkeeper will display your chances of combining success, on a scale of 1 to 5. The process of combining is not guaranteed, and some combinations are harder to complete than others. Your probability for success is dependent upon a number of factors, including the rarity of the items being combined and their difference in levels. Make note of your chance for success before proceeding.

You will be charged Taros for every combining attempt. If the combination fails, you keep your original items, but you still spend Taros. If the combination is a success, congratulations! Your two original items are replaced with a brand-new item.
Your character is rated on three values based on the quality of their equipment. They are:

Some things to remember about combining:
- Only weapons and armor can be combined (no accessories, gumballs or potions)
- Items in both the Style and Stats slot must be of the same type
- Items in the Style slot must be of the correct gender for your character
- Guide items cannot be placed in the Stats slot
- Combined items are not tradable
- Even if you fail a combining attempt, you can always try again

Once you have a new combined item, you may use it in a future combination, but only by placing it in the STYLE slot. Combined items are always identified with a special icon in your inventory so you can tell them apart from your other items.

You character is equipped with a new invention from Dexlabs called a NanoCom. The NanoCom combines navigation, communications and Nano storage into one easy-to-use device. When you use it, you see computer graphics superimposed over the world that will keep you informed as you battle the Fusion invasion.

* vs. One: How effective you are against a single enemy. This value is based on two things: 1) the weapon you have equipped in the first weapon slot, and 2) the original grouping of enemies.
* vs. Many: How effective you are when fighting two or more enemies. This value is also based on two things: 1) the weapon you have equipped in the first weapon slot, and 2) the original grouping of enemies. Note: the last monster remaining from an enemy group is still considered part of a multiple-enemy group.
* Defense: How effective you are at avoiding and absorbing attacks. This value is based on the individual Defense values of your shirt, pants and shoes.

* Communication Log: Record of recent communications and events that have happened near you.
* Equipped Nano: Shows which Nanos you have equipped, and if they have enough energy to be summoned.
* Your Health:  Displays your health status.
* Mini-Map: View of your immediate area from above.
Customize your controls using this window. To access your options, hit "ENTER" and then click on the "Settings" button.
Set the graphic resolution for the game, either in full screen or windowed mode. You can set the quality of effects to maximize your game's look or performance. You can also set sound volume here.
Choose display elements and colors. Customize the way damage, names, waypoints and other elements are displayed on your screen.
Allow requests from other players, like invites to group, trade or become a buddy. This is also where you review your blocked player list. Remove anyone from the list if you wish to see them again.

The higher your ranking numbers, the better your character is. Equipment will change these rankings. As your character levels up, you should make sure that your avatar is equipped with the best gear possible.
Customize your movement and interface commands to the keyboard keys and mouse buttons of your choice.
This guide is designed to help you learn about the details of the game. Click on the topic you want information about, then choose a subsection to read it.
This screen also displays your level and the guide character you are helping. More information about these is featured later in this document.

The column in the middle of the interface also shows what items you have equipped. The middle column also shows how many Weapon Boosts and Nano Potions you have. You can find out more about Weapon Boosts and Nano Potions in the Basic and Nano sections, later in this document.

On the right screen, you can see the items that you have collected in your pack. Note that you have tabs for "Equipment" and "Nanos" on the top of this section. You can look at the Nanos you own by selecting the "Nanos" tab.
The bottom right side of the screen displays counters showing how much Fusion Matter and Taros (money) you have.
To delete an inventory item, drag it to the trash can. But be careful! Once you do that, you will not be able to retrieve the item.
To close this window, press the ENTER key or click on the red button in the upper-right corner.
You are not alone in your adventure! When you start the game, I will guide you around the world until you leave the Future Zone.
If you opted not to skip the Future Zone, the first thing you should do is speak with me in Sector V (The Future). I will help you get started on your journey with your first world mission.

After you launch the game, you will see the character selection screen. To create a new character, click on the "Create New Character" button. If you want to use an existing character you have already created, click on that character's name, and then click the "Play" button.
I will also help you by sending you email alerts suggesting characters that could use your help. Your ingame email can be accessed with the “P” key.
To read the emails from your guide, hit "ENTER" and select "Email," or press the  P key.

When  your character reaches level 4, you are ready to return to the past and save the world. Once you use the repaired time machine and leave the future you will be asked to select a new guide to replace Computress. You can choose from the following four characters: Ben Tennyson, Dexter, Edd or Mojo Jojo.
Each guide will send you to contacts with missions and rewards that are available only to you and other players following that particular guide.

Change guides by contacting another guide directly or using a Guide Changing machine. This will cost you some Fusion Matter, depending on how often you are changing guides. You will not be able to use any item rewards given to you by one guide once you have switched to another guide.

Once your character is equipped, you can start exploring the world and get on with your mission to defeat Planet Fusion. You should start out by getting a mission from Computress in Hero's Square. Other characters (like Numbuh 108) have missions that will help you learn more about the game and how to get better equipment.

Characters with missions for you will have an exclamation point (!) mission icon over their heads. When you find a character with a mission, walk up to them until the talk icon appears, then click on it.

If the character has available missions for you, a list of the mission names will be displayed when you click on the talk icon. Likewise mission that can be updated with the character will also be listed. Just click on the one you are interested in.
During a mission you might be asked to contact other characters. These characters will have a question mark (?) mission update icon over their heads.
There are three types of missions available in the game:

* Guide Missions - Missions from your guide or guide contact.
* Nano Missions - Missions that will earn you a new Nano.
* World Missions - General adventuring missions available to all players.
You only get Nano Missions when you collect enough Fusion Matter to get the next level. Once you get enough, you will be automatically assigned a new Nano Mission.
Guide Missions are only granted by your chosen guide or his friends. You can not get Guide Missions from characters who are not associated with your guide.
World missions can be granted by any character, as long as you are the right level.
Once you choose a mission by clicking on it, the Mission Journal will pop up. It will give a mission summary and show you what the reward will be if you successfully complete the mission.
Each mission is broken down into tasks that have to be performed in sequence. Once you accept a mission, your current task is displayed in the Mission Journal.

If you are creating a new character, you will be taken to Dexlabs, where you have volunteered to help Dexter with a time travel experiment. The first thing you have to do is select your name and features using the tools provided.
You can open your Mission Journal at any time by either pressing the "J" key or pressing the "ENTER" key and selecting "Mission" from the main menu.
For detailed information about any of the missions in your journal, click on the mission and the details will pop up on the left side of the screen.

Click on the check box to the right of the mission name to make it your current mission, or click on the mission and then click "Make Current Mission". Your current mission displays a waypoint (red arrow) to the location of the next task on your Mini-Map to help you navigate. The current objective for the mission will appear under the Mini-Map.

The red waypoint arrow always points directly towards your target objective, but you might have to move around buildings, monsters and mountains to get to the final location. Always check the map to find your best route

Once you get close to your target the waypoint arrow will change to a red circle. If there is a "+"  (plus) sign in the circle, then your target is above you. If there is a "-" (minus) sign in the circle, then your target is below you.

entries.content.tabledata.mission.mission_string: no
Talk to Dee Dee.
I think Numbuh Two is the sweetest.
Grandpa Max just told me that he's located the other half of the energy cell that he needs for the surveillance satellite. It's inside the space port. Gear up and go.
Bet on Ben (Part 1 of 5)
Protect the Spaceport.
I'm so glad you're here. Fuse's monsters are everywhere and my Omnitrix is still acting up. Can you help us protect the Space Port?
I stopped some of the Thuggards and Clawbreakers from damaging our space program. We need to build spaceships to take the fight directly to Planet Fusion.
Hey, nice work on those creeps. You bought us some more time to work on these space ships. With any luck, the space port will be ours again soon.

We need to stop some of these Thuggards and Clawbreakers to keep them from trashing our rockets. The space ships we're building are the only way we're gonna be able to take the fight to Planet Fusion. Start by taking out six Thuggards.
Defeat six Thuggards.
Sweet. Now get five Clawbreakers.

We need to stop some of these Thuggards and Clawbreakers to keep them from trashing our rockets. The space ships we're building are the only way we're gonna be able to take the fight to Planet Fusion. You got those Thuggards, now get the Clawbreakers.
Defeat five Clawbreakers.
I recovered the positive node of the energy cell for Max.
Hey, that was some good stuff. Thanks!
Bet on Ben (Part 2 of 5)
Collect concentrated Fusion Matter.
The space port is in trouble. Concentrated Fusion Matter is leaking everywhere, and it's growing into mini-Terrafusers. Can you help us? I need someone fast.
Concentrated Fusion Matter fell onto the Space Port, and mini-Terrafusers started to grow. But I stopped them with Ben's Fusion Matter Absorber.
That's a relief. But we're not safe yet. Concentrated Fusion Matter has leaked into the atmosphere. We need to fix that.

A rain of concentrated Fusion Matter just fell on the space port. It's growing mini-Terrafusers, which will eventually become full-grown Terrafusers. We need to save our space ships and stop the infection from spreading.
Go into the space port infected zone.
The concentrated Fusion Matter is growing into mini-Terrafusers.
You need to collect the mini-Terrafusers inside the space port infected zone. You only have a short amount of time, or Fuse's infection will keep spreading!
Now Max has the positive node for the energy cell. Pretty soon he will be able to launch his surveillance satellite so we can study Planet Fusion more closely.
Collect first mini-Terrafuser.
You need to collect three mini-Terrafusers before time runs out.
Good work! Two more to go.
You need to collect the mini-Terrafusers inside the space port infected zone. You only have a short amount of time, or Fuse's infection will keep spreading!
Collect second mini-Terrafuser.
Great! Only one more left.
You need to collect the mini-Terrafusers inside the space port infected zone. You only have a short amount of time, or Fuse's infection will keep spreading!
Collect final mini-Terrafuser.
You did it! Nice job. Head on back to me.
The concentrated Fusion Matter has gotten out of control. You need to return to the starting point and try again.
Grandpa Max is trying to build a surveillance satellite that he will use to track Planet Fusion. You need to go to the space port in Offworld Plaza and look for the other half of the energy cell.
Return to starting point.
Wait, you need to go back to the beginning. The concentration levels are too high.
I know you can do it this time.

You collected the mini-Terrafusers inside the space port and stopped the infection from getting worse. But here's the bad news: I think the concentrated Fusion Matter has started to pollute our atmosphere.
Return to Ben.
You. I require your assistance.
Nice work out there. Stick around, I may need you for some more important stuff soon.
Bet on Ben (Part 3 of 5)
Use the Fusion Condenser on three infected areas.
The air over the space port has been corrupted by atomized particles of concentrated Fusion Matter. Will you assist your planet?
Go to the spaceport.

I used Vilgax's Fusion Condenser to keep the concentrated Fusion Matter from spreading through the atmosphere. But Mandark and Mojo are convinced that Vilgax is behind the spread of the concentrated Fusion Matter in the first place. Could they be right? Was it a mistake to help Vilgax?
Had you not assisted me, the consequences would have been dire. Now leave my presence.

The concentrated Fusion Matter has leeched into the atmosphere around the space port. If it continues to spread, the consequences to your planet will be catastrophic. Take the Fusion Condenser I built earlier and soak up the airborne particles of concentrated Fusion Matter from three strategically located points.
Go to Space Port infected zone.
Enter the infected area and use the Fusion Condenser. I've sent the coordinates.

The concentrated Fusion Matter has leeched into the atmosphere around the space port. If it continues to spread, the consequences to your planet will be catastrophic. Take the Fusion Condenser I built earlier and soak up the airborne particles of concentrated Fusion Matter from three strategically located points.
Go to absorption point one.
Why are you doing a mission for Vilgax? He's an alien, like Fuse!
Now use the Fusion Condenser on the absorption point.

The concentrated Fusion Matter has leeched into the atmosphere around the space port. If it continues to spread, the consequences to your planet will be catastrophic. Take the Fusion Condenser I built earlier and soak up the airborne particles of concentrated Fusion Matter from three strategically located points.
Look out. This area is tough. Be prepared for anything.
Use the Fusion Condenser.
Mandark, who is rarely right, happens to be right. In this case.
It's working. Now go to the next absorption point.

The concentrated Fusion Matter has leeched into the atmosphere around the space port. If it continues to spread, the consequences to your planet will be catastrophic. Take the Fusion Condenser I built earlier and soak up the airborne particles of concentrated Fusion Matter from three strategically located points.
Go to absorption point two.
Concentrated Fusion Matter landed when Vilgax got a Fusion Condenser!
Now use the Condenser on the second absorption point.

The concentrated Fusion Matter has leeched into the atmosphere around the space port. If it continues to spread, the consequences to your planet will be catastrophic. Take the Fusion Condenser I built earlier and soak up the airborne particles of concentrated Fusion Matter from three strategically located points.
Use the Fusion Condenser.
Condensed Fusion Matter would only come from one with a Fusion Condenser.
You need to defeat all of Fuse's bad guys and recover the energy cell Grandpa Max needs to complete his satellite.
Now proceed to the third and final absorption point.

The concentrated Fusion Matter has leeched into the atmosphere around the space port. If it continues to spread, the consequences to your planet will be catastrophic. Take the Fusion Condenser I built earlier and soak up the airborne particles of concentrated Fusion Matter from three strategically located points.
Go to absorption point three.
Plus, have you seen Vilgax's octopus face? It's pretty gross.
Use the Fusion Condenser again.

The concentrated Fusion Matter has leeched into the atmosphere around the space port. If it continues to spread, the consequences to your planet will be catastrophic. Take the Fusion Condenser I built earlier and soak up the airborne particles of concentrated Fusion Matter from three strategically located points.
Use the Fusion Condenser.
I have seen his octopus face, and agree that his octopus face is rather yucky.
Fools! I have heard every word! I will deal with you later. Bring me the Condenser!
You have successfully used the Fusion Condenser to absorb concentrated Fusion Matter from three strategically located points in the Space Port. Good. Now bring the device back to me.
Defeat the Clawbreakers.
Return the Fusion Condenser.
Go ahead and give the Fusion Condenser to Vilgax. I'll handle Mandark and Mojo.
You have prevented a serious calamity. Those fools Mandark and Mojo Jojo will soon learn the true meaning of disaster, however.
Imaginary Fusions (Part 1 of 5)
Defeat twelve Lazy Metal Boy Scouts.
I hate to trouble you, but some terrifying creatures have been creeping here from Prickly Pines. Will you defend us?
I defeated some Lazy Metal Boy Scouts that were menacing Foster's Home. So why was one of them carrying a roll of Toilet Paper?
Thank you for your laudable efforts. If only more youngsters were responsible like you, we might be free of this unseemly situation.

We've spotted terrifying Lazy Metal Boy Scouts lurking about the house. They've been creeping out of Prickly Pines and paying undue attention to our quiet little home. Could you go sweep up the nearest, say, dozen or so? That should keep them away from here.
Defeat 12 Lazy Metal Boy Scouts.
You did it. That's the other half of the energy cell! Quick, bring it to Grandpa Max.
Those ruffians will be near Camp Kidney. Give them the what-for.
Those creatures dropped some toilet paper!
Those Lazy Metal hooligans dropped some toilet paper. Please bring it to me!
Deliver TP to Mr. Herriman.
What would monsters need with THAT? Let me have a look.
Very strange to think about these monsters wandering about with errant rolls of toilet paper. Master Blooregard has taught me a thing or two about toilet paper. Let me think on this.
Imaginary Fusions (Part 2 of 5)
Find the traitor in Camp Kidney.
Would you believe that the toilet paper you recovered from the monsters contained a clue? Can you investigate it for us? Much appreciated!
I tracked Toiletnator to the outhouse where he was supposed to meet some of Fuse's cronies. He promised to give me the Plunger of Doom to use on Fusion Bloo.
You need to bring the positive node of the energy cell to Grandpa Max in Townsville Park. With both nodes, he should be able to complete his satellite.
Bravo! I daresay that Toiletnator fellow is a bit of a ne'er-do-well. It's disturbing to think that Fusion Bloo is lurking somewhere here in Foster's Home.

We found a hidden message on the roll of toilet paper. Invisible ink, apparently, revealed only when we treated the roll with lemon bathroom cleanser. The message says, "Meet me at the outhouse in Camp Kidney. Come alone." And it's signed by someone named Lou!
Go to Camp Kidney.
You must try to find the person named Lou that is mentioned in the message.
You need to find someone named Lou. He wrote a secret message to our enemies, and I won't tolerate this sort of tomfoolery!
Talk to Toiletnator.
I suppose you should talk to the man that's dressed up like an outhouse.
Okay, I'll admit it…Fusion Bloo tricked me into telling him how to get into Foster's through the plumbing. But I was gonna get him back and ambush him at the outhouse. Honest!
Oh, ho! It's time for some fisticuffs. I was quite a scrapper in my day. Defeat the Wild Skeeters and recover Toiletnator's Plunger of Doom.
Defeat the Wild Skeeters.
Pesky Problems
Deliver energy cell to Max.
Come to think of it, you might be a little more qualified for this task. Whadda you think? If you can get my Plunger of Doom back from the Wild Skeeters, you can keep it.
Great! Bring the plunger back here to me.
Bring the Plunger of Doom back to the Toiletnator. Please be hasty. I do not like to think about a Fusion Blooregard loose in the house.
Deliver plunger to Toiletnator.
Oh, dear! The handle appears to be broken. Come back to me soon and I'll have the handle fixed. This Plunger of Doom will get you right into Fusion Bloo's hiding spot. Promise!
If you are done with that odd bird in the toilet outfit, please come back to Foster's and speak to me.
Return to Mr. Herriman.
Very well, he appears to be telling the truth. Please come back to Foster's.
I am very concerned that a Fusion Blooregard is lurking somewhere about the house. Perhaps in a bathroom. This cannot be good…or very sanitary. Thank you again for your assistance.
Imaginary Fusions (Part 3 of 5)
With this energy cell intact, I will finally be able to complete my surveillance satellite. Imagine...we may be able to get a look at the surface of Planet Fusion.
Track down Fusion Bloo.
I know I promised that I'd give you my Plunger of Doom. It still needs a new handle. If you can get one back from Fuse's monsters, it's yours.
I reclaimed Toiletnator's Plunger of Doom and used it to find Fusion Bloo. Fusion Bloo says he'll help us if we protect him at Foster's Home for Imaginary Friends.
I told you the Plunger of Doom could do amazing things. Too bad that you didn't use it right. You better be careful. That Fusion Bloo is a trickster.
If you want to reclaim the handle for my Plunger of Doom, you will need to get it back from the Pack Arachnids nearby.
Defeat the Pack Arachnids.
Did you get it? Bring it back over here and I'll fix the plunger.
Bring the Handle of Doom back here to me and I'll fix the plunger for you.
Deliver handle to Toiletnator.
Great. If Fusion Bloo is hiding out inside one of the Foster's bathrooms, you can use this plunger to find him.
Okay, I'll admit it. You're good.
Take the Plunger of Doom back to Foster's and talk to Frankie. She should be able to help you.
Talk to Frankie.
So here's the Plunger of Doom! Make sure you tell everyone that the Toiletnator gave it to you and helped save the day. Even though I caused all of the problems to begin with…
A giant green weirdo called Fusion Bloo just locked us out of the house. He's asking to be adopted. As a duplicate of an imaginary friend, he says he deserves our protection. As if.
If you use the Plunger of Doom on the front door of Foster's, you should be able to get to Fusion Bloo.
Use plunger on front door.
Use the Plunger of Doom on the front door and FLUSH OUT the Fusion!
Heyyy…it didn’t work!
Why didn't the Plunger of Doom work? Why? I'll tell you why. You obviously don't know how to use it. Better you go talk to Frankie.
Return to Frankie.
You've done incredible work at the spaceport.
Come back here for a sec, and bring me that dumb plunger.
Fusion Bloo is not coming out. He says he'll help us if we promise to keep him safe. Do you think he's lying? Man, I just wanted to veg on the couch and watch TV…
Imaginary Fusions (Part 4 of 5)
Get Bloo to use the plunger.
I think I know how we can use this plunger, but we need Bloo's cooperation. He's down at the Dizzy World amusement park. Making himself useful, of course…

I brought the Plunger of Doom to Bloo at Dizzy World. He was the only one who could flush Fusion Bloo out of hiding. When I got back to Foster's, I found out that Bloo went after Fusion Bloo on his own!
Thanks for finding Bloo at Dizzy World. But now it seems that Fusion Bloo has maybe trapped Bloo inside the house. We need to get rid of that Fusion now!
Bring the Plunger of Doom to Bloo down at Dizzy World in City Point. I think he's the only one who can use it and get Fusion Bloo to leave the house. Hopefully, he'll cooperate.
Talk to Bloo at Dizzy World.
What?!? Frankie wants my help? Well, it does appear that the foot is on the other shoe now, doesn't it?
What's that smell? Toes?
Do whatever it takes, but get Bloo to come back here with that plunger. It's the only way to defeat Fusion Bloo.
Defeat six Dynamite Mice.
I will agree to help you…IF you defeat the Dynamite Mice that ate my lunch! Can you do that?
Very well. You may now come back to me and we can discuss terms.
Do whatever it takes, but get Bloo to come back here with that plunger. It's the only way to defeat Fusion Bloo.
Talk to Bloo.
I shall take this plunger and send Fusion Bloo back from whence he came! Meet me at Foster's and we shall emerge champions! Also, does this plunger do anything else super cool?
Well, that's the best we can hope for. Come back to Foster's and let's try to get this Fusion Bloo problem taken care of once and for all.
Return to Frankie.
I guess Bloo is on board with the plan. Come back to Foster's, okay?
You live the life of adventure!
You're not going to believe this. You gave Bloo the Plunger, and he came back here ahead of you and broke into the house. Fuse goo is everywhere and Fusion Bloo is still inside! Grrr!
Imaginary Fusions (Part 5 of 5)
Save Bloo and defeat Fusion Bloo.
Okay, I've had it. Fusion Bloo says he wants to be adopted, but he's totally full of it. And now he's got Bloo trapped inside. We gotta get rid of him.
Bloo was able to use the Plunger of Doom to get inside Fusion Bloo's hideout inside Foster's. I chased after them, saved Bloo and defeated the dangerous Fusion.
That was amazing! Thank you! We're so glad Fusion Bloo is gone. He was no Imaginary Friend, that's for sure. Now I just have to deal with cleaning up.
Bloo ran through here with the Plunger of Doom and entered the maze. I think that's where the entrance to Fusion Bloo's hideout is. I guess there's a way to get into the house through some pipes.
Find Fusion Bloo's lair.
Bloo ran through here with the Plunger of Doom and entered the maze. I think that's where the entrance to Fusion Bloo's hideout is. I guess there's a way to get into the house through some pipes.
Enter Fusion Bloo's lair.
Major Worry
Fusion Bloo has trapped Bloo inside the house! You need to defeat those Extremospawns to get the key that will free Bloo.
Defeat the Extremospawns.
Help!! I thought the Plunger of Doom would be cool, but this isn’t cool!
Quick! Bring the key here!
Quick! Take that key to free Bloo from Fusion Bloo's trap.
Use key on trap.
Thanks! That was a close one! I was totally going to defeat Fusion Bloo, but then all these monsters appeared and I accidentally remembered that I didn't want to die.
Please defeat Fusion Bloo so the house can get back to normal. Whatever "normal" is.
Defeat Fusion Bloo.
So you can defeat Fusion Bloo! Good luck!
Investigate Pokey Oaks for clues to Major Glory's location.
Great! You did it!
Great job beating Fusion Bloo. Well, get yourself out of there. It still seems weird to me that Fusion Bloo wanted to become a resident of the house. Even if he was lying…it's pretty strange!
Exit the area.
Better get out of there…Bloo really left the place a mess.
Fusion Bloo sure is annoying!
Fuse appears to be obsessed with the Imaginary Friends.
Maybe Fuse should get an imaginary friend of his own.
Great job beating Fusion Bloo!
Treetop Troubles (Part 1 of 3)
Defeat Bladed Mantises.
I hear Dexter is trying to track down some missing super heroes. Major Glory's last known appearance was at a "career day" event at Pokey Oaks Junior High.
Welcome to the Jungle Outpost of Ed, king of the jungle! We found some weird candy and the Bladed Mantises stole it. So can you get it back?
I helped the Jungle Outpost get rid of some Bladed Mantises, plus I recovered some Crazy Brain Candy.
Ed the Jungle King says that you have done most excellently and your good deeds will be remembered througout the land. Also, I'm itchy.

My kingdom is in peril! The dreaded Bladed Mantises came upon us and took some of that weird candy we found that makes people go crazy and stuff. It tastes terrible, so don't eat it. Just get it back.
Defeat the Bladed Mantises.
That's it! You got it! Bring it here to me. So sayeth the king.

My kingdom is in peril! The dreaded Bladed Mantises came upon us and took some of that weird candy we found that makes people go crazy and stuff. It tastes terrible, so don't eat it. Just get it back.
Return the Crazy Brain Candy to Ed.
Thank you for your helpful help. Those Bladed Mantises will learn not to trifle with the likes of me or the likes of you. Or the likes of us together.
Treetop Troubles (Part 2 of 3)
I found Major Glory's day planner in Pokey Oaks.
Defeat seven Ghoulish Growths.
Hey, I heard how you helped that Ed kid. This jungle is a dangerous place, and Fuse's nitwits make it even more dangerous. Can you help, mate?
I fought Ghoulish Growths and Rabid Arachnids and helped protect the Jungle Outpost.
Nice work, mate. Them Ghoulish Growths and Rabid Arachnids are pretty tough. But you did some nice work.
